To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
M(1)-muscarinic receptors activate PLC, PKC, and Ca(2+), which in turn control N, L, and P/Q Ca(2+) channel types in neostriatum.

(1) M(1)- and M(4)-class receptors modulate L, P/Q and N-type Ca(2+); channels; (2) M(1) receptors control L-, N-, and P/Q-types of Ca(2+).channels via PLC/PKC signaling pathways; and (3) M(1).receptor modulation of N- and L-types of Ca(+) channels, but not P/Q-type, is blocked by the PKC inhibitors, whereas
muscarinic modulation via M(1)- and M(4)-receptors is mediated by different signaling pathways, and that M(1) receptors modulate L-, N- and P-Q-type Ca(2+ )channels via PKC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the signaling pathways that control Ca(2+) channel modulation in neostriatum.
the mechanisms by which the muscarinic M1 receptor can modulate N and L types, as well as the P/Q type, Ca(2+) channel in neostriatum.

a better understanding of the mechanisms of modulation of Ca(+)2 channels by muscarinic receptors, and the results obtained here are relevant for the study of the mechanisms underlying learning and memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M(1) receptors, via PLC, activate PKC and PP2B in neostriatum.
M(1) receptors modulate all three types of Ca(2+ )channels in neostriatum, via PLC, PKC and intracellular calcium, and that PKC is the only kinase involved in this modulation.

M(1) receptors control L, N and Q/P Ca(2+) currents in neostriatum, via a signaling cascade that involves PLC activation, PKC and intracellular calcium, and that this signaling cascade is not shared by the D(2)-type receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
M(1) receptors modulate L, P/Q and N Ca(2+) currents via a PLC/PKC pathway, while M(2) receptors modulate N and P/Q Ca(2+) channel via a G protein pathway.

in neostriatum, muscarinic modulation through M(1)-, D(2)-, and M(2)-receptors is controlled by different branches of the PLC/PKC pathway, and that M(1) and M(2) receptors control N and P/Q-type channels via G-proteins and L-type channels via PKC.

in neostriatum, muscarinic modulation is mediated by the activation of PLC and PKC, and that the modulation of different Ca(2+), channel types can be mediated by different branches of the PKC signaling cascade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the M(1) muscarinic receptors modulate all three Ca(2+) channel types in neostriatum neurons.
muscarinic modulation is a very versatile and complex mechanism that is used to regulate different types of Ca(2+).channels in the same cell.
